title: Grateful Dead Live at Danish Center on 1966-03-12

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture with pitch quirks still delivers a raw, blues‑heavy ’66 set highlighted by an epic Viola Lee Blues and Pigpen’s powerhouse vocals.
ai_review.review: The three‑song excerpt showcases the early Dead at their tightest, with Pigpen’s soulful blues shouting, a marathon Viola Lee Blues and a fun Midnight Hour that even includes Garcia’s horn‑imitating solo. The soundboard source is generally clear and well‑mixed, but listeners note speed/pitch anomalies, a near‑silent drum track and an abrupt cut‑off on Midnight Hour. Overall the performance shines despite the technical oddities and labeling confusion.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (high show quality) while noting several recording issues (pitch, mono folding, drum level). Weighted average of show (~4.5) and recording (~3.2) yields a ~4.1 star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mix is generally crisp, but several tracks run fast/slow (Viola Lee needs -4% pitch correction), some are folded to mono, drums are almost inaudible, and Midnight Hour ends abruptly.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A short, blues‑focused three‑song burst that feels tight and energetic; despite the mislabeling, the sequence flows well with strong vocal call‑and‑response and extended improvisation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia delivers a lively solo on Midnight Hour (even mimicking a Martha & the Vandellas horn line) and shares vocal call‑and‑response moments with Pigpen.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum track is very low in level, almost inaudible, though the band overall feels tight.
